questions.question: Explain budding in yeast.
questions.solution_html:
• At the time of budding small portion of cell wall at or near one pole of yeast cell softens and
  • thins, protoplast in this region bulges out in the form of outgrowth or protuberance
  • gradually increase in size known as bud. As the bud forms nucleus of the parent cell divides
  • with its vacuole. One of the daughter nuclei along with daughter vacuole migrates into the
  • enlarging bud. Bud grows and becomes constricted at the base, cytoplasm of bud and
  • mother cell remains continuous for some time, then the opening between the two cells
  • close, separating the cells leaving a scar on both cells. A scar with convex surface remains on
  • mother cell, daughter cell retains a concave birth scar (3). Diagram (2)
